evidence: The original planScopes built `new Set(scopes.flatMap(s => s.files))` and only checked under-assignment, while the scout prompt promised 'exactly ONE scope'; 9e9de8a added duplicatePaths detection plus a warning log.
guidance_note: When a prompt asserts an 'exactly one' invariant, check both bounds in code (none and more than one), not just the one the feature needs.

evidence: Same gap as F1, raised by a different scope: the 'exactly ONE scope' upper bound went unchecked. Both threads were closed by one fix in 9e9de8a.

The repo contract told the model add_scope takes 'exactly two fields' while the collector schema always declared optional `files`. 9e9de8a dropped the field count ('providing:') and updated the test to assert no count claim.
guidance_note: When prompt text describes a tool's parameters, describe them the way the tool schema does; don't add a count or exclusivity claim the schema doesn't enforce.

evidence: Flag is a false positive for caused_by: 9e9de8a was named as the fix for F1-F3, but the EXCLUDE_PATTERNS override that copies the lock-file defaults was unrelated new work bundled into that commit, not part of any fix. The agent took the reviewer's option (b): the comment names action.yml as the source to keep in sync.
guidance_note: Don't bundle unrelated new config (here the dist/** exclude) into a commit named as a review fix; it widens the next round's surface and blurs fix attribution.

evidence: Flag false positive: 9e9de8a did not touch test/collector-smoke.test.js. The hunk shows the original PR rewrote scope 2's focus and kept only name and files assertions; b7517ca restored the focus assertion.
guidance_note: When rewriting a test fixture, keep every assertion the old test made on the changed record.

evidence: 9e9de8a (the F1/F2 fix) added a pass-level `log('⚠️ scout assigned ... to more than one scope')` in runMultiScopePass but tested only planScopes; the swept-path warning already had a pass-level test in 'runMultiScopePass — scout coverage sweep'.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a new log or effect next to an existing one, add the matching test at the same level the existing one is tested.

evidence: Flag false positive: parseScopeValue's coerce-to-[] is original PR code, and b7517ca touched only a workflow comment and tests. The pushback holds: a non-array files becomes [], so in PR mode those paths are swept into the catch-all and the 'scout left N changed file(s) unassigned' warning fires. The slip is visible, though the warning names it as unassigned rather than malformed.

The reviewer concedes 'The production call path always goes through parseScopeValue, which guarantees files: []'. The missing guard is a state the enforcer makes unrepresentable, and planScopes is original PR code, not touched by b7517ca.
The `!duplicatePaths.includes(p)` dedup guard was written in 9e9de8a as the F1 fix, but that commit tested only the two-scope overlap. 755812a added the three-scope case.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a dedup or once-only guard, test the case that exercises the guard (three or more members), not only the case that passes without it.

evidence: The same-reference early return `if (sweptPaths.length === 0) return { scopes, sweptPaths }` predates the PR (it appears as a removed line in the hunk). The reviewer itself says no caller mutates the result, so there is no defect.

This re-raises F4's duplicated lock patterns on the comment b7517ca rewrote. F4 was resolved by documenting the copy rather than removing it, so the reviewer flagged it again. Declining is defensible: the list is small and stable, and a stale copy still excludes dist/** plus the old lock files.
guidance_note: When a fix deliberately keeps a known duplication, record the reasoning so a repeat flag can be answered by pointing to it rather than relitigated; better, add the cheap sync assertion the reviewer offered.

evidence: The O(n×d) `duplicatePaths.includes(p)` scan was introduced by the F1 fix in 9e9de8a. The reviewer admits the impact is negligible, so this is a style nit rather than a real performance bug; 6ada691 swapped in a Set.
guidance_note: In fix code, use a Set for membership the first time instead of Array.includes inside a loop; it costs nothing and closes off this nit.

evidence: Flag false positive: 6ada691 touched only planScopes. The prompt line '... (3) keep it to one or two sentences. List that group's changed files in the scope's "files".' is original PR code, and it contradicts 'do THREE things'.
guidance_note: When appending an instruction to a prompt that counts its items, update the count or keep the new instruction out of the counted list.

narrative: Three fixes for F1 each drew a follow-up finding: the pass-level log was untested (F6), the three-way dedup was untested (F9), and Array.includes was used in a loop (F12). The fix commit 9e9de8a also carried an unrelated EXCLUDE_PATTERNS change, which drew F4 and then F11 when that duplication was documented rather than removed. Rounds 2 and 4 still surfaced original-code issues (F7, F8, F10, F13). Round 3 was entirely fix-caused or a repeat. The agent's pushbacks (F7, F8, F10, F11) were sound.
guidance_observations: The F1 fix shipped new code (a dedup loop and a pass-level log) with only one unit test, and the next two rounds were spent adding tests and a Set for that same fix.
Bundling unrelated workflow config into a review-fix commit added a new finding thread that ran across two rounds.
